title: Orchid and Elen's Wobbly Stage
markdown:
Down where the soft sand lay like a velvet blanket on the ocean floor, and moonlight shimmered in lazy waves, lived two neighbours. There was Orchid, a kind octopus, always busy with clever ideas. She loved to make whirring things from pebbles and shells, but she often wondered if anyone noticed her wonderful creations. Her other neighbour was Elen, a crab who was, well, a little bit grumpy. She liked her quiet corner of the seafloor just so, and all the bustling and wiggling made her want to retreat.

The Tide Festival was coming, a special time when sea creatures gathered to celebrate the moon and waves. Singing corals made soft music, and glowing algae danced. One soft morning Orchid whispered, “Oh, Elen, I have a grand idea. Let’s build a stage for the festival. A stage everyone will marvel at.”

Elen clicked her claws, a sound like pebbles tumbling in a gentle tide. “A stage? Hmmph. Seems like a lot of bother, Orchid,” she rumbled. “And who will marvel? Just the little fish and the sleepy starfish, I suppose. Always something new to fuss over.” She liked her quiet home best.

“Everyone, dear Elen. It will be made of the shiniest shells from the deep where light plays tricks, and draped with the longest, silkiest seaweed that whispers secrets to the waves. Come, help me. It will be a marvelous place for anyone who wishes to share a song or a story.” She nudged Elen gently with a soft tentacle, her voice full of hope.

So, with Orchid’s nimble arms and Elen’s sturdy claws, they began. Orchid found smooth pearly shells that gleamed. Elen, with a sigh like seafoam, helped arrange them just so. She was good at making things lie flat and secure. They wove in soft green seaweed that draped like a velvet curtain, smelling of the cool deep ocean. It was a wobbly wonderful stage, truly a marvel. It tilted just a little and swayed with the currents, giving it a gentle personality.

As they admired their work, a little shimmer caught Orchid’s eye. Then another, and another. A small shoal of tiny fish, no bigger than your thumb, with scales like scattered rainbows, had drifted near. Their eyes were wide with silent wonder, and they swam in gentle circles, watching Orchid and Elen with innocent fascination. They seemed to whisper to each other with flickers of their fins.

“Oh dear,” Elen grumbled, scuttling closer to her familiar rock. “What do they want? Always something new. This is why I like my quiet corner. They’ll be wanting to jump and splash all over our lovely stage.” She imagined the carefully placed shells being bumped out of place.

The fish didn’t speak, of course. They simply watched, their little fins fluttering with quiet excitement. Their movements mirrored the gentle ebb and flow of the water. They seemed utterly captivated by the shimmering stage and the two builders, as if a grand performance was already underway. Orchid felt a familiar flutter of shyness deep within her soft body.

Then a most curious thing happened. The little fish, perhaps inspired by the gentle rhythm of the waves or the sparkling shells, began to swim in patterns. They wiggled and swirled, weaving in and out with surprising grace. It looked like a dance, a gentle ballet of scales and fins, a performance born from pure joy.

Orchid watched, her eyes wide with amazement, her shyness forgotten. “Elen, look. They’re dancing. They’re dancing on the currents. Oh, perhaps they want to join the festival.”

Elen clicked her claws a little louder this time, a sound of rising worry. “Join? Dancing? On our stage? It’s already wobbly enough with just us, Orchid. Imagine all those wiggling bodies. It’ll be a complete muddle. My shell might get scratched.” She imagined her precious shells scattering and her quiet day ruined.

Soon more fish arrived, drawn by the soft music of the waves and the enchanting sight of their fellows twirling. The shoal grew, a shimmering ribbon of silver and blue. Their enthusiastic dance made the whole stage sway a little more, a gentle undulation. Elen felt a wave of nervousness wash over her. “Orchid,” she huffed, her voice strained, “this is far too much commotion. My nerves are not made for such hullabaloo. It’s simply too much excitement for one day.”

Orchid looked at the happy dancing fish, their scales flashing like tiny jewels. She looked at Elen, whose shell seemed to grip the sand tighter. She remembered her own quiet worries about being noticed and saw the same hopeful energy in the fish. She felt a little flutter of stage fright herself, her eight arms feeling tangled.

“Now, Elen,” she said, her voice like a calm tide pool. “They’re not trying to cause trouble. They are simply filled with joy, and they want to share it, just like we wanted to share our beautiful stage. We built it together, and perhaps we can let them dance too.” She nudged Elen gently. “It’ll be alright. We’ll make sure it holds. We are quite good builders, you and I.”

Elen looked at the cheerful fish, their little mouths opening and closing in gleeful sighs. She looked at Orchid’s kind face. Hmmph. It was rather a lovely sight, she had to admit, even if it was a little bit noisy and a tad wobbly. “Oh, very well,” she mumbled, trying to sound grumpy, but a small secret smile played on her lips. “But no sudden movements, mind you. And if anyone bumps into me, I shall scuttle away.”

And so the Tide Festival began. The little fish danced their shimmering dance upon Orchid’s wobbly wonderful stage. They twirled and swirled, a rainbow of happy motion. The stage held strong, thanks to Orchid’s careful work and Elen’s watchful eye. Even Elen found herself tapping a claw to the rhythm of the waves, a tiny happy sound. The festival was a marvel, filling the water with unexpected joy.

As the moonlight grew softer, painting the seafloor in shades of pearl and silver, and the last of the fish drifted away, winking goodbye like tiny lanterns, Orchid and Elen sat together on their stage. It was quiet now, the only sounds the gentle lapping of the waves, a peaceful lullaby. Orchid felt a warm glow of pride. Elen felt a pleasant peace settle deep in her shell. They looked up at the vast starry sky, a gentle blanket of dreams stretching above them. And soon, just like the tide pulling back to rest after a long happy day, they too felt ready to drift off to slumber, safe and sound on their marvelous wobbly stage, the gentle currents rocking them softly to sleep.
